name: curl
summary: Sends HTTP requests (and much more) from the terminal.
description: Transfers data from or to a URL. By default, curl makes a GET request and prints the response to standard output; you need -o or -O to save it. It is the go-to tool for testing an API: method (-X), headers (-H), request body (-d). It also handles HTTPS, FTP, SFTP and other protocols.

options.description: Saves the response to this file.
Saves the response under the file name found in the URL.
Shows only the response headers (HEAD request).
Shows the response headers before the body.
HTTP method: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE…
Adds a header, for example "Authorization: Bearer …".
Request body; implies POST. @file reads the body from a file.
Sends JSON: adds the right Content-Type and Accept headers.
Hides the progress bar and errors.
Fails (non-zero exit code) if the server answers with an HTTP error.
Details the whole exchange: connection, TLS, headers sent and received.
